title: RAW UNREVIEWED: same written head with different attached characteristic letters expands to different following words
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Cappelli section5.62 supplies specific printed pairs with the same h or marked ut head but different superscript letters, yielding different following words. Preserve these finite source relations and an ordinary final superscript-s countercase when bounding a historical writer. This is source-only contract evidence, not a general multiword insertion law or a target reading.

design.mechanism: Some attached letters are characteristic letters of a following lexical word, while the visible head contributes the preceding word; exact host-plus-exponent combinations retain finite source-attested expansions.
design.unit: Four specified printed form-expansion pairs in Cappelli section5.62 p35, preserving all depicted marks, with section5.45 p33 as the literal-letter countercase.
design.contrast: A writer restricted to exactly one expanded lexical word per attached written group versus a finite source-scoped relation permitting these particular two-word expansions. Neither global exponent-only meaning nor arbitrary phrase insertion is proposed.
design.prediction: A writer claiming coverage of this declared source family must represent hoc modo versus hoc nomen under the same visible h head, and ut dicit versus ut probatur under the printed ut head. It must also preserve the raised final s in patris as a literal letter, not force omitted content at every elevated glyph. These are observed source obligations, not held predictions or new scored tests.
design.scope: Printed handbook source only. No CoReMA incidence claim, native manuscript dating or global rule induction; no Voynich glyph, word, hidden space, language, reserve, fit or decoder. All source exposure is disclosed development evidence.

design.smallest_present_action: Use the four exact pairs and literal-s countercase in the active source contract reconstruction to declare its coverage honestly. A word-internal writer may remain a local writer, but cannot claim this broader family. No experiment is needed to test an already printed inequality of word counts.
design.changed_research_decision: Determines whether a proposed historical writing relation is explicitly source-local or claims phrase-abbreviation coverage; prevents extending a one-word residual channel merely because marker position is known. It does not choose a target interpretation.
known_counterexamples: Section5.45 explicitly gives ordinary final superscript s, with a twelfth-century qualification.
The top of p35 has single-word superscript expansions; elevation alone cannot select multiword scope.
The four paired examples do not prove an independent oo=modo rule, global compositionality or a finite inventory of all medieval phrase abbreviations.
CoReMA B4/Gr1 ex nodes were reported without spaces in their existing contract; the handbook does not create corresponding cases in those source bodies.

design.dependency: Before any target descendants, establish a shared source writer and an actual target construction with unequal written consequences; confirmed words are not a logical prerequisite, but free per-word assignments would not provide the required shared rule.
